name: Andaz West Hollywood
positioning: Rock-history hotel on Sunset Boulevard, the first hotel on the Sunset Strip and the former Riot House, with a rooftop pool
best_for: Music fans drawn to the hotel's Riot House rock history
Travelers who want a Sunset Strip base with Hollywood Hills or city views

facts.text: Andaz West Hollywood was the first hotel on the Sunset Strip.
The hotel is at 8401 Sunset Boulevard in West Hollywood.
Condé Nast Traveler notes that rockers including Led Zeppelin and Guns N' Roses stayed here, when the hotel was nicknamed Riot House.
Condé Nast Traveler notes the hotel's rock history is commemorated through modern framed prints.
Guest rooms feature local art on the walls and Calcutta mosaics in the bathrooms.
Sunset Boulevard View rooms have floor-to-ceiling windows and a separate sunroom area with a desk.
Hollywood Hills View rooms look out over the Hollywood Hills.
The Andaz Suite King has a marble bath with a separate rain shower and a tub.
The Penthouse Suite has views of the Hollywood Hills and a private balcony.
Riot House Restaurant has an open kitchen and menus that change seasonally.
Riot House Bar, once a hangout for rockers of the 1970s, is a place to drink, snack and socialize on Sunset Boulevard.
The hotel's Pet Program provides a dog bed, two bowls and a treat bag.

highlights.text: The Rockstar Room is a deluxe room designed around the hotel's Riot House history, with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the Sunset Strip.
The Presidential Suite was designed by Jonathan Adler, with furnishings from his Modern American Glamour Collection.
The Panorama Suite has views of the Sunset Strip, the Hollywood Hills and downtown Los Angeles, with two bedrooms and a private balcony.
Condé Nast Traveler notes the hotel's pool is on the roof.
The Sundeck rooftop pool bar has views of the Sunset Strip and the Hollywood Hills.

considerations.text: The Sundeck rooftop pool bar is open seasonally.
Condé Nast Traveler notes the hotel sits in an unassuming building on Sunset Boulevard and seems slightly removed from the action at first glance.
WhataHotel notes the urban location can bring street noise.
